Sanjay Shadija vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 August, 2024 
Author: Narendra Kumar Vyas Bench: Narendra Kumar Vyas  1/3  2024:CGHC:31701  NAFR  HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH AT BILASPUR  CRR No. 933 of 2024   Sanjay Shadija S/o Shri Keshoomal Shadija (Wrongly Mentioned As  Keshmool Shadija) Aged About 45 Years Proprietor Sehat Brand  Farman Flour (Pecked), M/s Bhawani Aata Chakki, Daldal Shivani,
 Mova, Raipur, District Raipur, Chhattisgarh.
 ... Applicant  versus   State Of Chhattisgarh Through The Food Safety Officer, Food And  Cosmetics, Janjgir, District Janjgir-Champa, Chhattisgarh. 
 ... Respondent For Applicant : Mr. Paras Mani Shriwas, Advocate For Respondent/State : Mr. Karan Bahrani, Panel Lawyer Hon'ble Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order On Board 21.08.2024 1. The applicant has filed this present criminal revision under Section 438/442 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 being aggrieved with the order dated 23.07.2024 (Annexure P/1) passed by the learned Sessions Judge Janjgir, District - Janjgir-Champa (C.G.) in Criminal Appeal No.
26/2024 by which learned Sessions Judge has dismissed the appeal as not maintainable. 
2. Learned Sessions Judge while dismissing the appeal has recorded its finding that as per Section 17 or 68 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, the appeal has to be preferred before the Food Safety and Standard Tribunal, as such, the appeal was not maintainable before it. It has been further observed by the learned Sessions Judge that under the Act the Collector has been appointed as Adjudicator and against that order an appeal can be preferred before the Tribunal only. As such also the appeal is not maintainable.

1 3. This Court has directed the Registry of this Court to place on record whether any notification has been issued in pursuance of notification dated 09.10.2017 issued by the Government of Chhattisgarh, Department of Food and Civil Supplies. It has been brought to the notice of this Court that a memorandum has been issued by Registrar General of this Court on 17.11.2017 appointing all the District and Sessions Judge of every Civil District Court as Presiding Officer of the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal. The operating part of the order reproduced below :- 
"On the subject cited above, I am to enclose herewith a copy of notification no.
F-25-8/2011/IX/55 published in the Chhattisgarh Gazette on 09.10.2017 and inform you that the State Government ha established the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal in every Civil District for Civil territorial jurisdiction of that district to hear the appeals from the decision of the Adjudicating Officer working in the concerned district under Section 68 of the said Act, and has appointed the District and Sessions Judge of every Civil District as Presiding Officer of the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal established as above."
4. Since the High Court has already issued memorandum dated 17.11.2017 appointing the District Judges as Appellate Authority, the impugned order passed by the learned District and Sessions Judge, Janjgir-Champa is set aside. The matter is remitted back to the learned Sessions Judge,
District Jangjir-Champa who will decide the appeal by performing as Food Safety Appellate Tribunal under the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006. 
5. With the aforesaid observation and direction, present criminal revision is disposed of. 
6. Memorandum dated 17.11.2017 be also sent to the concerning District Judge for onward compliance. 
Sd/-
